brief:
# BRIEF-GATE-SPEAKS — a gate that fails must name what failed, on stderr

**Status:** DRAFT, dispatch-ready. Authored 2026-08-16 by Waffles.
**Scope:** gate scripts only. No product code, no test changes, no gate SEMANTICS changes.
A leg that is red today stays red; a leg that is green today stays green. This changes only
what the script SAYS when it fails.

## The defect, measured

aion records a failed run's `failure_reason` from the declared command's STDERR. Today, for a
server-run gate, that field reads verbatim:

> the declared command `zsh` exited 1 with no standard error output

while three named red legs sit on disk in the same directory, fully diagnosed.

**Census, with a planted control.** Denominator: 32 files matching `gate*.sh` across
`stack/aion` and `apps/manifold` (excluding node_modules). Of those, **0** write any summary
to stderr. Canary proving the instrument is live and the idiom is native to this estate:
**254** shell files in those same two trees DO use `>&2`. Instrument: `/usr/bin/grep`, no
`2>/dev/null` on the sweep. So the absence is a real property of the population, not a
broken search.

**Positive control that the reporting layer is NOT at fault.** Same field, same server, same
day (2026-08-16): of 9 Failed rows, **5 carry the error text verbatim** — including a
`norn_dev` row ("activity engine failure: activity response channel dropped") and a
`due_diligencer` row quoting crawlberg's own argv error — and **4 report silence**, all four
of them gate-script runs (4c4ef686, 38633615, 5b33e73d, 7e2192df). It is not the workflow
type and it is not aion's field. aion's `failure_reason` works. The gate scripts are mute.

## The mechanism, at the bytes

Specimen: `apps/manifold/gate-logs/read-path-leg1/gate.sh` (read in full).

- `:28` — `echo "$name=$code"` — per-leg results ARE emitted, to **stdout only**.
- `:15` — `typeset -a LEG_CODES` — the accumulator stores **codes, never names**.
- `:48-51` — the failure path:
  ```
  for code in "${LEG_CODES[@]}"; do
    (( code != 0 )) && exit 1
  done
  exit 0
  ```
  It exits 1 **saying nothing at all**, and because the array dropped the names, at the moment
  it decides to fail it is **structurally incapable** of naming which leg failed. It held that
  fact one line earlier and discarded it.

So `>&2` alone is NOT the fix. Two things are wrong: the accumulator is lossy, and the failure
path is silent.

## Requirements

R1. **The accumulator keeps names.** Replace the code-only array with name+code pairs
    (e.g. `LEG_RESULTS+=("$name=$code")`). Per-leg stdout output at `:28` is unchanged —
    existing readers keep working.

R2. **The failure path speaks, on stderr, naming the failures.** Before `exit 1`, emit to
    stderr a single summary naming EVERY non-zero leg and its code, plus the log directory
    where each leg's full output lives. Not a count. Named legs. The success path stays
    silent — a green gate has nothing to say.

R3. **Fixed across the population, not the specimen.** All 32 gate scripts. Some use a
    different accumulator shape or exit structure — adapt per file rather than pattern-
    substituting blind; a sed across 32 files is a rejected approach here. State the per-file
    disposition, including any file where the shape does not apply and why.

R4. **RED-FIRST FIELD PROOF, and it must be the real path.** The oracle is the OPERATOR'S
    ACTUAL COMMAND, not a unit test: run a gate through the aion server with at least one leg
    forced red, then read that run's `failure_reason` back out of `aion list` and show it
    naming the failed leg. Commit the before/after text. A gate whose summary is proven only
    by running the script in a terminal has NOT been proven — the whole defect is that the
    terminal path and the server-recorded path differ.

R5. **Do not change what any gate decides.** Exit codes, leg selection, and pass/fail
    semantics are untouched. Demonstrate this: for one script, show an unchanged green run and
    an unchanged red exit code across the change.

## REQUIRED: Census controls
R3's denominator is the 32 files above, re-derived by the builder with its own instrument (do
not inherit my number — re-count and report if it differs). Positive control: the 254 files
already using `>&2` prove the search works. Per-file label including UNEXAMINED. No
`2>/dev/null` on the sweep.

## REQUIRED: Numbers
Every count carries its counter. 32 and 254 are MY measurements at 2026-08-16 — re-derive.

## REQUIRED: Absence claims
"No gate script writes a summary to stderr" carries its search (instrument + scope + canary)
in the delivery report.

## REQUIRED: Refusal surface
n/a — this adds disclosure, refuses nothing new.

## REQUIRED: Timing sensitivity
Not timing-sensitive.

## Hard constraints (estate law)
Worktree only; the manifold main checkout serves the live kernel — never build there. NEVER
push; landing is the dispatcher's re-gate on the final tree. Live estate ports
(4176/41100-41102/9490s) and every `.manifold*` path untouchable. No new dotfolders, no
daemons, no CARGO_TARGET_DIR override.

## Done means
R4's server-recorded `failure_reason` names a failed leg, with before/after committed; all 32
files dispositioned; R5's no-semantics-change demonstrated; delivery report states plainly any
file left unchanged and why.

## Why this is worth its own dispatch
It was deliberately NOT bolted onto the mailbox-disposal brief, whose scope cut is explicit
and narrow. Gate scripts are infrastructure every other brief's "gates green" requirement
depends on; folding an infrastructure fix into a scoped product brief would be exactly the
scope drift that brief refuses. Small, orthogonal, independently gateable — its own leg.


=== DISPATCH ADDENDUM (Waffles, 2026-08-17, supersedes the brief's numbers) ===

POPULATION CORRECTION. The brief's census of 32 was contaminated: its find
never excluded .worktrees/, so worktree duplicate copies were counted. The
true population in THIS repository at your worktree's commit (ab6284f7e) is
17 tracked gate*.sh files — re-derive it yourself inside your worktree and
report your number. My measurement of the defect at dispatch: 17 files, all
parse under zsh -n, 16 contain no stderr write at all, 1 already complies.
The apps/manifold specimen the brief's mechanism section reads is 1 further
file in a DIFFERENT repository — it is OUT of this run's scope and will be
fixed in its own run; your disposition table covers this repository only.

SCOPE OF THIS RUN. Your working directory is an aion worktree on branch
gate-speaks. Fix every gate*.sh in the tree per R1+R2, adapting per file
(R3 — no blind seds). Commit to your branch as you go. Commit nothing outside
the gate scripts and your report.

REFERENCE IMPLEMENTATION, IN YOUR TREE. gate-logs/console-live-fleet/gate.sh
is the 9a89091 shape authored from birth: named accumulator
(LEG_RESULTS+=("$name=$code")), failure summary on stderr naming every red
leg + its code + its log path, silent success. Read it before writing. Note
its subshell-not-command-group comment: under zsh, `{ ...; exit 1; } > log`
runs in the CURRENT shell and an exit inside kills the whole script silently
— the exact defect this brief eliminates. Do not introduce it while fixing.

R4 RULING (dispatcher's). The server-path mechanism (gate stderr →
failure_reason) is already FIELD-PROVEN by run 21b9ea9a on 2026-08-16:
before-text "the declared command `zsh` exited 1 with no standard error
output", after-text "GATE RED — 3 of 6 legs failed: ..." recorded in the
server's own failure_reason. You do not need to re-prove the server path.
Your R4 duty is per-file honesty: for ONE representative script you modified,
run it in a terminal with one leg forced red and capture stdout and stderr
SEPARATELY (> out 2> err), showing the summary lands on fd 2 and names the
leg. Include the capture verbatim in your report.

R5 UNCHANGED. For that same script also show: a green run stays exit 0 with
silent stderr, and the forced-red run's exit code is what it was before your
change.

REPORT. Write gate-logs/gate-speaks-run/report.md in your worktree (the gate
checks it exists and is non-empty): your re-derived population count with its
instrument, the per-file disposition table (every file: fixed / already
compliant / shape-does-not-apply with why), the R4 capture, the R5
demonstration, and your absence-claim search per the brief's REQUIRED
sections. Reply with the same report verbatim.
